paper_title: DLP Dynamic Layerwise Pruning in Large Language Models
caption_used: Comparison of per-output and per-layer perplexity at different sparsity rates using a logarithmic scale. Both pruning configurations maintain comparable perplexity below 10^1 for sparsity rates up to 50%, after which values begin to diverge. At 60% sparsity, the Per-Output configuration reaches approximately 15 while Per-Layer remains near 10^1. The most pronounced separation occurs at 70%, where Per-Output perplexity climbs to roughly 50 while Per-Layer reaches approximately 25. At 80% sparsity, both configurations approach 10^3, with Per-Output exhibiting marginally higher perplexity than Per-Layer at this extreme.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: Диаграмата илюстрира сравнение на перплексията (perplexity) при два различни подхода за подрязване — „Per-Output" и „Per-Layer" — при различни нива на разреденост (sparsity rate) в контекста на големи езикови модели. Хоризонталната ос е етикетирана като „Sparsity Rate" и съдържа осем категории, подредени в нарастващ ред: 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70% и 80%. Вертикалната ос е етикетирана като „Perplexity" и използва логаритмична скала, обхващаща диапазон от приблизително 10⁰ до 10³, с пунктирани хоризонтални линии, маркиращи нивата при 10¹, 10² и 10³. За всяка категория на разреденост са представени два стълба, групирани един до друг: синият стълб съответства на конфигурацията „Per-Output", а оранжевият — на „Per-Layer", както е указано в легендата в горния ляв ъгъл на диаграмата. При нивата на разреденост от 10% до 50% и двата стълба остават с относително ниски стойности, под нивото на 10¹, като височините им са визуално много близки помежду си. При 60% разреденост стълбите започват да нарастват забележимо, като синият стълб („Per-Output") достига приблизително 15, а оранжевият („Per-Layer") остава близо до 10¹. При 70% разреденост синият стълб се издига до приблизително 50, а оранжевият — до около 25–35. При 80% разреденост и двата стълба достигат стойности, приближаващи се към 10³, като синият стълб („Per-Output") е незначително по-висок от оранжевия („Per-Layer"). Стълбите не са подредени по височина, а следват нарастващия ред на категориите по хоризонталната ос, като няма допълнителни визуални акценти като засенчване, удебеляване или анотации върху отделните стълби.
model_annotations.Chinese: This grouped bar chart compares the perplexity of two pruning configurations—Per-Output and Per-Layer—across different sparsity rates, as indicated by the title context from the paper "DLP Dynamic Layerwise Pruning in Large Language Models." The horizontal axis represents the Sparsity Rate, with categories labeled at 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80%, arranged in ascending order from left to right. The vertical axis represents Perplexity and uses a logarithmic scale, spanning from approximately 5 (just below 10¹) up to 10³, with dashed horizontal gridlines at 10¹, 10², and 10³. At each sparsity rate category, two bars are grouped side by side: a blue bar on the left representing "Per-Output" and an orange bar on the right representing "Per-Layer," as identified by the legend in the upper left corner of the chart. At 10% sparsity, both bars are very short and nearly identical in height, each reaching a perplexity of approximately 5. At 20% and 30%, the bars remain similarly short and closely matched, still near a value of approximately 5. At 40% sparsity, both bars grow slightly but remain below 10¹, with values around 6. At 50%, the bars increase modestly, with both still near or just below 10¹, approximately 7 to 8. At 60% sparsity, the bars begin to show more visible separation; the blue Per-Output bar reaches roughly 15 while the orange Per-Layer bar is near 10 to 12. At 70%, the separation becomes more pronounced, with the blue Per-Output bar climbing to approximately 50 and the orange Per-Layer bar reaching roughly 25 to 35. At 80% sparsity, both bars rise dramatically toward 10³; the blue Per-Output bar reaches approximately 600 and the orange Per-Layer bar reaches approximately 900, with the Per-Layer bar appearing marginally taller than the Per-Output bar at this extreme sparsity level. The bars appear to be ordered by increasing sparsity rate along the horizontal axis, and no individual bars are visually emphasized through special shading, bolding, outlines, or annotations beyond the standard blue and orange color coding.
model_annotations.English: This bar chart illustrates the comparison of perplexity values between two pruning configurations—Per-Output and Per-Layer—across different sparsity rates, as described in the context of dynamic layerwise pruning in large language models. The horizontal axis represents "Sparsity Rate" and contains eight categorical labels ordered from left to right: 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80%. The vertical axis represents "Perplexity" and uses a logarithmic scale, ranging from approximately 5 (just below 10^1) up to 10^3, with dashed gridlines at 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. The chart uses grouped bars, with each sparsity rate category containing two side-by-side bars: a blue bar on the left representing "Per-Output" and an orange bar on the right representing "Per-Layer," as indicated by the legend in the upper left corner. At 10% sparsity, both bars are very short and nearly identical, each reaching approximately 5 on the perplexity scale. At 20% and 30%, the bars remain similarly low, both hovering around 5 to 6. At 40% sparsity, the bars are still close together and slightly taller, reaching roughly 6 to 7. At 50%, both bars remain below 10^1, with values near approximately 7 to 8. At 60% sparsity, the bars begin to show more visible separation, with the blue Per-Output bar reaching approximately 15 and the orange Per-Layer bar reaching approximately 10 to 12. At 70% sparsity, the separation becomes more pronounced, with the blue Per-Output bar climbing to roughly 50 and the orange Per-Layer bar reaching approximately 25 to 35. At 80% sparsity, both bars rise dramatically, with the blue Per-Output bar reaching approximately 500 to 600 and the orange Per-Layer bar reaching approximately 800 to 900, both approaching 10^3. The bars are arranged in ascending order of sparsity rate from left to right, and the progressive increase in bar height follows the increasing sparsity rate. No bars appear to be visually emphasized through bolding, outlining, or annotation beyond the standard color coding.
model_annotations.German: Das Diagramm vergleicht die Perplexität zweier Pruning-Konfigurationen – „Per-Output" und „Per-Layer" – bei unterschiedlichen Sparsity-Raten und verwendet dabei eine logarithmische Skala. Die horizontale Achse zeigt die Sparsity Rate mit Kategorien von 10 % bis 80 % in Schritten von 10 Prozentpunkten, während die vertikale Achse die Perplexität auf einer logarithmischen Skala darstellt, die von etwa 10⁰ bis 10³ reicht, mit gestrichelten Hilfslinien bei 10¹, 10² und 10³. Für jede Sparsity-Rate sind zwei Balken nebeneinander gruppiert: ein blauer Balken für „Per-Output" und ein orangefarbener Balken für „Per-Layer", wie in der Legende oben links angegeben. Bei einer Sparsity Rate von 10 % liegen beide Balken bei einem Wert knapp unter 10¹, wobei sie nahezu gleich hoch erscheinen. Bei 20 % und 30 % zeigen beide Konfigurationen ebenfalls sehr ähnliche Werte, die weiterhin knapp unter 10¹ liegen. Bei 40 % steigen die Werte leicht an, bleiben jedoch noch unterhalb von 10¹. Bei 50 % erreichen beide Balken Werte, die sich 10¹ annähern, wobei der blaue Balken geringfügig höher als der orangefarbene erscheint. Bei 60 % Sparsity erreicht der blaue „Per-Output"-Balken einen Wert von ungefähr 15, während der orangefarbene „Per-Layer"-Balken bei etwa 10¹ verbleibt. Bei 70 % steigt der blaue Balken auf einen Wert von ungefähr 50 und der orangefarbene auf etwa 25 bis 35. Bei 80 % Sparsity nähern sich beide Balken dem Bereich von 10³, wobei der blaue „Per-Output"-Balken einen Wert von ungefähr 500 bis 600 erreicht und der orangefarbene „Per-Layer"-Balken einen Wert nahe 10³ aufweist. Die Balken sind nicht in einer sortierten Reihenfolge nach Wert angeordnet, sondern folgen der aufsteigenden Reihenfolge der Sparsity-Rate-Kategorien auf der horizontalen Achse, und es sind keine besonderen visuellen Hervorhebungen wie Umrandungen oder Annotationen an einzelnen Balken erkennbar.
